goldens.comment: In .topic-meta-data h5 a, the original code had color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) but was changed to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)). The lightness for the light theme changed from 30% to 70%, which is a dramatic inversion

This change for desktop/user.css changes $primary from 30% to 50% for the light theme; most other changes preserve the original $primary value and move the complement to $secondary for dark. Consider reviewing this (also applies to a similar .name change in the mobile variant).
In topic-post.css the original code used $lightness: 70% but the replacement uses $lightness: 30% for the light theme. This makes the text significantly darker than intended.

The light theme color for `.topic-meta-data h5 a` was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, which may unintentionally reduce contrast and affect readability. This change should be reviewed to ensure it aligns with design intentions.
In mobile/user.scss line 497, the lightness value for dark themes should be inverted to 70% instead of being changed to 50%. This change may lead to unintended visual regressions in light themes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss:102 — The bulk replacement reverses the intended shades, changing the light theme from 70% to 30% and the dark fallback from 30% to 70%.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for mobile/modal.scss line 102, the change is from `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%);` to `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%));`. This is inconsistent with the pattern used throughout the rest of the diff, where typically the light theme uses a higher lightness value for $primary (like 70%) and the dark theme uses a complementary value for $secondary. Here the light theme argument uses 30% (darker) while the dark theme uses 70% (lighter), which appears to be reversed compared to the original intent and the pattern in other files. For example, in desktop/modal.scss line 50, the same selector uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))` which is the opposite order.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss:182 — The bulk replacement silently changes the light-theme title shade from 20% to 50% and gives dark themes the wrong 50% fallback.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss around line 179-182, the change is from `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%);` to `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%));`. The finding correctly identifies that: 1) The light-theme value changed from 20% lightness to 50% lightness (a significant visual change), and 2) The dark-theme fallback uses 50% lightness on $secondary. This is inconsistent with the pattern used elsewhere in the diff where 20% lightness on $primary typically corresponds to 80% lightness on $secondary (e.g., line 244 in the same file shows `$lightness: 20%` paired with `$lightness: 80%`). This appears to be an unintentional change that alters the appearance.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss:291 — The light-theme branch changes this link from primary lightness 30% to 70%, so the theme-specific replacement regresses the existing desktop appearance.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at line 291 in desktop/topic-post.scss, the diff shows: `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%));` - The first argument to dark-light-choose is for light theme, and it's using 70% lightness. The original code was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%);`. So the light theme value changed from 30% to 70% lightness, which is a significant visual regression for the existing light theme appearance. This is a real bug where the replacement doesn't preserve the original light-theme behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/user.scss:522 — The group-member name now uses 50%/50% rather than preserving its 30% primary lightness and a 70% secondary dark branch.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/user.scss around line 522, the change shows `.name` selector going from `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The finding correctly identifies that the original 30% lightness for primary was changed to 50%/50%, which is inconsistent with the pattern used elsewhere in the codebase where 30% primary typically pairs with 70% secondary (as seen in many other changes in this diff like user.scss lines 119, 125 which use 30%/70%). This appears to be an unintentional inconsistency that changes the visual appearance.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss:102 — The mobile message-length color inverts the intended lightness pair to primary 30% and secondary 70%, changing both light and dark rendering from the original 70% primary intent.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows at line 102 of mobile/modal.scss the change from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. This is inconsistent with the pattern used throughout the rest of the diff, where typically when converting from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: X%)` the pattern is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: X%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 100-X%))`. Here the original was 70% lightness on primary, but the new code uses 30% on primary (inverted) and 70% on secondary. This appears to be a mistake that would change the appearance in light mode from a light gray (70% lightness) to a darker color (30% lightness).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss:182 — The mobile preview heading is changed from 20% primary to 50%/50% instead of retaining its 20% primary and 80% secondary theme mapping.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss around line 179-182, the h3 selector shows: `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%));` replacing `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%);`. The finding correctly identifies that the original was 20% lightness on primary, but the new dark mode mapping uses 50%/50% instead of the expected pattern of 20%/80% that would maintain visual consistency. This is inconsistent with other similar changes in the diff (e.g., desktop/topic-post.scss line 318 uses 20%/80% for similar h3 styling). This appears to be a genuine inconsistency/bug in the theme mapping.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss:291 — No light/dark compiled-CSS regression test covers this conversion, so the unintended light-theme 30%-to-70% change is untested.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims there's an 'unintended light-theme 30%-to-70% change' at line 291. Looking at the diff, line 291 shows: `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%));` which was changed from `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%);`. The original was 30% lightness on $primary. The new code uses dark-light-choose with 70% for light theme and 30% for dark theme. This is actually a deliberate pattern change - the light theme now gets a lighter color (70%) while dark theme gets 30% on $secondary. This appears to be an intentional design decision consistent with other changes in the diff, not an 'unintended' change. The claim about missing regression tests is generic advice not grounded in specific diff content.
